profile_text.body:
OpenAI is a for-profit AI company founded in 2015 and headquartered in San Francisco, California. Its primary consumer product is ChatGPT, described on the company's site as a tool to "answer questions, write, create images, complete work, and code," available for free or via a downloadable app. The company also offers the OpenAI API and GPT models on a usage-based pricing basis, a Playground and Dashboard environment for API testing and fine-tuning, and specialized products including the DALL-E image generation model, the Sora video generation model, and the Whisper API for speech recognition, transcription, and translation. Operator, listed as an autonomous web agent with browser control capabilities, rounds out the product portfolio.

OpenAI carries a notable legal footprint, with at least 187 matters recorded under California exposure and active cases across multiple federal courts. Named cases include suits filed in the Northern District of California (Starr v. OpenAI Group PBC, Byrd v. OpenAI, Inc., and Craddock v. OpenAI OpCo LLC), the Southern District of New York (wikiHow, Inc. v. OpenAI, Inc.), the Southern and Northern Districts of Florida, the District of Hawaii, and the Eastern District of Arkansas, as well as an appeal pending before the Ninth Circuit brought by X.AI Corp. against OpenAI. The Florida Attorney General's office also appears as a plaintiff in a case in the Southern District of Florida against OpenAI Global, LLC.

Several MCP servers referencing OpenAI are registered in the site's registry, covering image and audio generation tooling, authenticated and orchestration agents built on LangChain, structured output agents, and academic paper search integrations, reflecting broad third-party developer activity around OpenAI's APIs.
